minutes.headline: Personnel Committee approved hiring an IT administrative assistant at grade eight, but job descriptions and pay grid are not final.
minutes.summary: The committee approved the HR Director's recommended hire of an IT administrative assistant, then spent most of the meeting on the unfinished job descriptions and the proposed pay grid. Members said the draft grid would cut pay for most SAP employees, so it is unacceptable as drafted and the consultant must rework it. They discussed rescheduling around absences and decided to keep the March 6 meeting.

budget_items.topic: Pay for new IT administrative assistant
budget_items.what_was_said: The HR Director gave the hire's grade and step and an hourly rate. This is a single-person position with no similar roles in the group.
A member said the draft grid would lower pay for most SAP employees at the middle and upper steps, which was not the intent. Members agreed the grid needs rework before submission.

budget_items.topic: Comp plan impact for Finance Committee and Select Board
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said the grid and its impact are what the Finance Committee and Select Board care about most, and the impact of the comp plan has yet to be seen.
A member asked what happens if the grid pays an SAP role more than a union clerk. The response was that this is a collective bargaining matter outside the Personnel Committee.

decisions.decision: Joanna will act as chair until reorganization after June 30, per the Charter.
HR Director will work with the consultant that week to get the job descriptions and grid back on track.
The March 6 meeting stays as scheduled; a Thursday meeting was floated but not adopted.
Members to send job description feedback to the HR Director by Thursday so the consultant can revise over the weekend; revised grid to go in the Dropbox.
Draft job descriptions are not private, so a member may let her husband see them, though they are not final.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted unanimously to hire an IT administrative assistant at the grade and step the HR Director recommended.
Members said the draft SAP pay grid would lower pay for most SAP employees at the middle and upper steps, which was not the intent, and agreed it needs rework.
The HR Director will work with the consultant that week to get the job descriptions and the grid back on track.
The committee kept the March 6 meeting as scheduled; a Thursday meeting was floated but not adopted.
Members are to send job description feedback to the HR Director by Thursday so the consultant can revise over the weekend.

why_it_matters: The SAP pay grid sets pay for a class of town employees and feeds the compensation plan, so a draft that lowers pay for most of them is a payroll and staffing matter before it is a budget one.
Members said the Finance Committee and Select Board care most about the grid and its impact, so the cost of the plan has not yet been shown to the bodies that fund it.
watch_next: The March 6 Personnel Committee meeting, where revised job descriptions and the reworked grid are expected.
The revised grid, which is to be placed in the Dropbox after the consultant's weekend revision.
